questions.q: What most separates a top-level writer's effect answer from a middle-level one?
options: Effects of individual words are explained and linked into an overall impression
The meaning of every choice is given
questions.why: Middle answers explain meanings with general effects; top answers explore specific words and how images work together.

questions.q: "The old station slept under a blanket of snow." Which word is personification?
questions.why: "Slept" gives the station a human action; "blanket" is a metaphor, not personification.

questions.q: A student writes: "The simile creates a vivid image." What is the best way to improve it?
options: Add "and makes the reader want to read on"
Explain what the comparison makes the reader picture or feel, and why
questions.why: General comments that fit any text earn little; explain the specific effect.

questions.q: "Waves gnawed at the foot of the cliff." Explain the meaning and effect of "gnawed".
questions.model: Meaning: the waves wear away the cliff slowly and constantly. Effect: "gnawed" suggests a hungry animal chewing, so the sea seems persistent and destructive and the cliff seems vulnerable.
points: effect: animal / hunger connotations – relentless, destructive sea
